nodes.prompt:
TASK: Dispatch exactly ONE bounded ChatGPT Web helper batch (two implementation workers) for the orca-lite parity fix and capture its authoritative terminal result.
PREP: the batch manifest exists at /tmp/orca-parity-fix/manifest.json (labels: orca-fix-backend, orca-fix-frontend; workspace /Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite). Read it first.
DISPATCH (single invocation, no other helper processes):
  mkdir -p /tmp/orca-parity-fix/reports
  jq -c /tmp/orca-parity-fix/manifest.json | /Users/indo/code/project/omo-bridge/target/release/delegate_to_chatgpt_web --batch-stdin --json
Run it as a background session and rely on the native completion notification (no polling loops, no duplicate watcher processes). Take ONE early peek at the session output to catch an immediate hard-reject (ok:false / invalid_arguments / rate-limit); if hard-rejected, report the verbatim error and stop.
Do NOT pass --browser-driver (discovery is cmux-first with Orca fallback). Do NOT pass --close-on-terminal (IDLE_RETAINED default). Do NOT resume or close any pre-existing scope - this run is a fresh batch by design. Do not spawn a second helper process for any reason, including retries; implementation runs take a long time (an hour or more is normal - do not treat silence as failure).
DELIVERABLE:
1. The helper's complete terminal stdout saved verbatim to /tmp/orca-parity-fix/helper-output.json.
2. Each worker's final summary extracted into /tmp/orca-parity-fix/reports/<label>.md (the terminal JSON carries status; the rich final summaries live in the task-state JSONs under ~/.omo/bridge/task-state/ for the new scopes - locate by matching the new scope ids and copy the final notes/summary content; say so if you did).
3. Final message: per worker - label, scope_id, terminal_state, session_state, and a digest of its summary (per-item status, commits, test counts); plus where the full reports live.
SCOPE: you own only /tmp/orca-parity-fix/**. Never edit repository files; never touch browser tabs or scope files outside the helper contract.
VERIFY: the helper exits 0 and every worker reached ready=true before actual dispatch (visible in early output or ~/.omo/bridge/delegation-lifecycle/ entries for the new scopes); the terminal JSON parses as JSON.
STOP WHEN: the helper's terminal JSON is saved and both worker summaries are extracted, or the helper returns an authoritative terminal error (report it verbatim and stop - do not retry).

nodes.prompt:
TASK: Run the four verification gates against the CURRENT working tree of /Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite after the Web implementation batch reached terminal state, and record exact results.
DELIVERABLE: /tmp/orca-parity-fix/local-gates.txt containing, for each command: the exact command line, exit code, pass counts, and verbatim first failure if any. Also explicitly confirm (with the verbatim test-name lines from gate 3 output) whether the new lease-semantics tests exist and pass (names containing e.g. split/last-tab/spawn-count/lease semantics from the D1/D2 increment), and list the git log of new commits (git log --oneline) plus per-commit changed-file summary (git show --stat) to prove no commit touched files outside its owner's scope (backend commits: only src-tauri/**; frontend commits: only ui/** and PERF_NOTES.md).
Commands (from /Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite, each to completion; background sessions + completion notifications, never poll loops, never duplicate a running command):
1. cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml
2. cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings  (if it finishes suspiciously fast from cache, re-run once with CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/orca-parity-fix/clippy-target to prove the local crate was linted)
3. bun run --cwd ui test
4. bun run --cwd ui build
SCOPE: READ-ONLY on the repo (never edit/fix/stash/checkout/commit; vite writing ui/dist is the build's own output and fine). You may create files only under /tmp/orca-parity-fix/.
VERIFY: recorded exit codes match actual command exit statuses; excerpts are verbatim.
STOP WHEN: all four exit codes plus the D1/D2 test-name confirmation and the commit-scope audit are recorded in local-gates.txt and your final message.

nodes.prompt:
TASK: Fan-in verdict for the orca-lite parity-fix run: decide per audit item D1-D11 whether it is now fixed, partially fixed, not fixed, or legitimately blocked (with reason), and whether the run introduced any regression.
INPUTS (read all):
- /tmp/orca-parity-fix/local-gates.txt (gates + D1/D2 test-name confirmation + commit-scope audit)
- /tmp/orca-parity-fix/helper-output.json and /tmp/orca-parity-fix/reports/*.md (worker summaries)
- /Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite/ORCA_LITE_PARITY_AUDIT.md (the defect list with file:line evidence and completion conditions)
- /Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite/ORCA_LITE_PARITY_FIX_EXECUTION.md (pinned design decisions: mirror split, last-tab serialization, worker split)
- The repo working tree at /Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite (read-only)
VERIFICATION STEPS:
1. Per-item verdicts D1-D11 with evidence you PERSONALLY re-opened (file:line). For D1 specifically verify the pinned model: single-tab split creates a mirror pane with NO spawn (check the store code path AND the test asserting zero spawn calls), last-tab replacement awaits close confirmation before spawning, and the lease contract is encoded in the test fakes.
2. Re-open at least 5 load-bearing citations from EACH worker report; a failing citation flips that row to "unverified claim".
3. Commits: git log the new commits; per commit confirm (git show --stat) it touched only its owner's paths; confirm the two baseline commits captured the pre-existing dirty layers (backend: manager.rs+mod.rs nested-root fix; frontend: the 11 staged ui files) and that the working tree is now clean of those pre-existing modifications.
4. Regression check: the 5 previously-fixed items from the audit (spawn_in_worktree present, e2e destructive delete, WriterLeaseGuard used, ipcErrors module exists + tests, createWorktree contract match) still hold - quick greps.
5. Sample re-run: bun run --cwd ui test yourself; record exit code and counts.
6. Gates: read all four results from local-gates.txt; a gate failure fails the run.
DELIVERABLE (final message): per-item table D1-D11 (verdict | evidence | notes); regression list; gates summary; overall PASS/FAIL verdict with a Korean summary paragraph; explicit list of anything still requiring runtime (macOS GUI) proof; a per-scope recommendation (keep retained for follow-up vs safe to close) using the scope_ids from helper-output.json.
SCOPE: READ-ONLY everywhere; write nothing to disk.
VERIFY: every table row carries a citation you re-opened or a gate output you read from the artifacts.
STOP WHEN: the per-item table + gates summary + overall verdict + scope recommendations are complete.
